vision-roadmap.name: Vision to Roadmap
vision-roadmap.summary: Connects a compelling long-term vision to near-term executable plans, bridging aspiration and action.
vision-roadmap.description: Connects a compelling long-term vision to near-term executable plans, bridging aspiration and action. Open with a specific three-to-five-year North Star, honestly diagnose the gap between today and that vision, organize the strategy into two to four named pillars, show the phased roadmap with milestones and dependencies, and end with concrete, assigned first steps for the next 30-90 days. The tone is inspirational and strategic: it creates shared direction and commitment to a plan. Best for strategic planning, annual kickoffs, product strategy, and OKR launches; typical decks run 8-20 slides.

beats.name: Vision
beats.description: State the 3-5 year North Star. It should be specific, memorable, and directional rather than generic.

beats.name: Current State Gap
beats.description: Honestly assess where you are today versus the vision. The gap justifies the plan.
beats.instructions: Define the gap between today and the vision.

beats.name: Strategic Pillars
beats.description: Organize the strategy into 2-4 named priority themes. Each pillar should be independently compelling.
beats.instructions: Name the strategic pillars that close the gap.

beats.name: Roadmap
beats.description: Show the phased execution plan with timeframes, milestones, and dependencies. Gantt or swim lane formats work well.

beats.name: First Steps
beats.description: Close with concrete, assigned actions for the next 30-90 days. Remove the gap between inspiration and execution.
beats.instructions: Identify the immediate moves that start execution.

regulatory.name: Regulatory / Compliance
regulatory.summary: Government agencies, auditors, or compliance bodies reviewing adherence to rules and standards.
regulatory.description: Government agencies, auditors, and compliance bodies reviewing adherence to rules and standards. Lead with evidence, date-stamp material, cite document references, and map each claim to the requirement it satisfies. Moderate chart density; 20-40 slides with an appendix.

all-hands.name: All Hands
all-hands.summary: The full company — mixed roles, mixed seniority, looking for context, signal, and inclusion.
all-hands.description: An all-hands audience spans the whole company. Frame the period in terms anyone can grasp: what we did, what mattered, and what's next. Highlight people and teams; surface successes and challenges; close on a forward-looking note. Avoid lapsing into function-specific jargon.

align.name: Align
align.summary: Create shared understanding and commitment across people who need to move together.
align.description: Use when stakeholders need a common view of goals, constraints, priorities, or responsibilities. Emphasize shared language, explicit tradeoffs, and next steps.
align.outcome: Stakeholders leave with the same priorities and operating assumptions.
successCriteria: Owners and next steps are clear

formal.name: Formal
formal.summary: Polished, restrained voice for board, investor, and regulator audiences.
formal.description: Authoritative without being cold. Use third-person constructions, full sentences, and concrete numbers. Avoid hedges and humor that depend on shared in-jokes; rely on clarity and precision to land.
voiceCues: Use third person and the corporate 'we' sparingly.
Lead with the recommendation, then evidence.
Quote concrete numbers; avoid round-tripping ranges.
Prefer full sentences to bullet fragments on key claims.
samplePhrases: Q4 revenue grew 18% year over year, led by enterprise expansion.
We recommend approving the Series B raise at $30M.
Net retention was 124%; gross retention was 96%.

classic.name: Classic
classic.description: A timeless, clean, and versatile theme with balanced color contrasts and classic typography. Ideal for professional, readable presentations.

burnt-orange.name: Burnt Orange
burnt-orange.summary: Warm orange and red accents for energetic commercial decks.
burnt-orange.description: A warm, high-contrast palette built around burnt orange, red, navy, and gold. It feels active without losing structure.

cool-horizon.name: Cool Horizon
cool-horizon.summary: Cool blue-green palette tuned for professional business decks.
cool-horizon.description: A balanced cool-toned scheme with deep navy, business blues, and teal accents. It works well across strategy, finance, and technical narratives.

pt-serif.name: PT Serif
pt-serif.description: PT Serif is a sans serif OPF font scheme for Latin presentations, using PT Serif for both headings and body text.

tenorite.name: Tenorite
tenorite.description: Tenorite is a sans serif OPF font scheme for Latin presentations, using Tenorite Display for headings with Tenorite for body text.

cover.name: Cover
cover.summary: The opening slide: title, subtitle and an optional picture.
cover.description: Open a presentation with its subject and a short introduction. Add a picture when it helps establish the context.

text.name: Text
text.summary: Prose. Several blocks sit side by side when short and stack when long.
text.description: Explain one idea in continuous prose. Use paragraphs or flowing blocks for detail that needs to be read in sequence.

chart.name: Chart
chart.summary: One to six charts, with an optional note.
chart.description: Give a chart enough space to show its evidence. Use the title to state the conclusion and labels to explain the measures.

table-beside.name: Table beside
table-beside.summary: A table with commentary beside it.
table-beside.description: Place a table beside its interpretation. Use the supporting text to explain the conclusion without repeating every cell.

timeline.name: Timeline
timeline.summary: Dated events or a roadmap along one axis, with optional notes.
timeline.description: Show events or milestones in chronological order. Label each item with a date or stage and a concise description.

list.name: List
list.summary: Bulleted or numbered points; one long list flows into columns.
list.description: Present several related points in a clear sequence. Use bullets for independent points or numbered items for an ordered list.
